I've investigated this further, and we can't route this specific error in our error handler since it's outside of our routing/encapsulation model.
A solution could be doing the same thing we are doing for the 404 handling and tracking the context so we can access the error handler, but it seems overkill.
For now, I would keep this pr as is, since we are already doing a very similar thing in other places, such as the client error and the graceful shutdown.

issue_context.title: 404 with not encoded URI path parameter
issue_context.body:
## 🐛 Bug Report

If I send a wrong path parameter without appling an `encodedURI` I get a 404 response and a warn:

```
{"level":30,"time":1570179820901,"pid":21956,"hostname":"MSPIGOLON5591","reqId":3,"req":{"method":"GET","url":"/%25what%","remotePort":53476},"msg":"incoming request","v":1}
{"level":40,"time":1570179820902,"pid":21956,"hostname":"MSPIGOLON5591","reqId":3,"msg":"the default handler for 404 did not catch this, this is likely a fastify bug, please report it","v":1}
{"level":40,"time":1570179820902,"pid":21956,"hostname":"MSPIGOLON5591","reqId":3,"msg":"ÔööÔöÇÔöÇ / (ACL|BIND|CHECKOUT|CONNECT|COPY|DELETE|GET|HEAD|LINK|LOCK|M-SEARCH|MERGE|MKACTIVITY|MKCALENDAR|MKCOL|MOVE|NOTIFY|OPTIONS|PATCH|POST|PROPFIND|PROPPATCH|PURGE|PUT|REBIND|REPORT|SEARCH|SOURCE|SUBSCRIBE|TRACE|UNBIND|UNLINK|UNLOCK|UNSUBSCRIBE)\n    ÔööÔöÇÔöÇ * (ACL|BIND|CHECKOUT|CONNECT|COPY|DELETE|GET|HEAD|LINK|LOCK|M-SEARCH|MERGE|MKACTIVITY|MKCALENDAR|MKCOL|MOVE|NOTIFY|OPTIONS|PATCH|POST|PROPFIND|PROPPATCH|PURGE|PUT|REBIND|REPORT|SEARCH|SOURCE|SUBSCRIBE|TRACE|UNBIND|UNLINK|UNLOCK|UNSUBSCRIBE)\n","v":1}
```

## To Reproduce

```js
const fastify = require('fastify')({ logger: true })
fastify.get('/:strangeId', (req, reply) => {
  reply.send({ strangeId: req.params.strangeId })
})
fastify.listen(3000)
```

```
curl -X GET   http://localhost:3000/%what%   -H 'Accept: */*'   -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate'   
-H 'Connection: keep-alive'   -H 'Host: localhost:3000'   -H 'User-Agent: PostmanRuntime/7.17.1'
```

All work with an encoded path param:

```
curl -X GET   http://localhost:3000/%25what%25   -H 'Accept: */*'   -H 'Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate'   
-H 'Connection: keep-alive'   -H 'Host: localhost:3000'   -H 'User-Agent: PostmanRuntime/7.17.1'
```

## Expected behaviour

I wouldn't expect a 404.

With a plain server, the URL is:

```
{ req: '/%what%' }
{ req: '/%25what%25' }
```

```js
const http = require('http')
const server = http.createServer(function manageResponse (req, res) {
  console.log({ req: req.url })
  res.end('hello')
})
server.listen(3000)
```

## Your Environment

- *node version*: 12
- *fastify version*: 2.9
- *os*: Windows
comments:
This looks like a bug that might originate from find-my-way.

cc @delvedor

This happens because [fast-decode-uri-component](https://github.com/delvedor/fast-decode-uri-component) instead of throwing an error returns `null`, and because of that `find-my-way` [will call the default route](https://github.com/delvedor/find-my-way/blob/8cb73484d39d531ee7cf5b6735323e6b80985014/index.js#L334-L340).
Then in Fastify, we call the 404 handling, which can't handle that route as well, since also the 404 will get a 404.
This is not a bug in `find-my-way`, but it's instead something we are not handling correctly in Fastify.

> { req: '/%what%' }

According to https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percent-encoding

> Because the percent character ( % ) serves as the indicator for percent-encoded octets, it must be percent-encoded as %25 for that octet to be used as data within a URI.

so the request path is wrong and 404 is fine.

~~But `%` is part of ASCII and can be used in the URI e.g `http://localhost:3000/%=+`. `%` is only relevant as escape char.~~

~~IMO we must not handling everything starting with `%` as escape sequence so the bug is sitting in `fast-decode-uri-component`.~~

Update: `%` must be escaped as described above.

I know the URL was wrong, but with some path param, it is hard to spot if the variable is a business domain value that I wasn't aware of.

> but it's instead something we are not handling correctly in Fastify.

I would prefer a "500 unparsable path params" to avoid confusion instead of 404
Just for reference: Hapijs has the exact same behaviour as fastify and expressjs throws an error `URIError: Failed to decode param '%deded'`. I agree with @Eomm we should produce a different error.
I agree that we should produce an error, but it's not our fault, so it should be in the 4xx family *(400 should work)*.
FWIW Express sends back a 400 for the Express error listed above.
`400` makes sense because the request is not valid. But I think `500` also makes sense because the server encountered an error when parsing. 🤷‍♂

I've opened https://github.com/delvedor/find-my-way/pull/134, which is the first step for supporting this feature in Fastify core.
Give it a look!
I've opened https://github.com/fastify/fastify/pull/1888 with the fix, let's continue the discussion there :)

I am still getting error log this with fastify 3.14.2 for the following request

```
http 'localhost:3000/%c0'
```

> updated to fastify 3.17.0, same result

This is quite old issue, please open a new one with a [Minimal, Reproducible Example](https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example)?

Without it, we are unable to help you.

review_comments: Should we document that behaviour anywhere?

As a general rule, I think we should document as much as possible, but since this is an internal configuration which (currently) cannot be configured by the users, I'm not sure we need to document it, and if so, where?
Shouldn't this be configurable? Some people may not be using Fastify as an `application/json` only server.

Good point, but we are already doing the same in other parts of the framework.
https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/0aef7f323a79835ae6529a4f72c90744a731c74e/lib/route.js#L291-L297

https://github.com/fastify/fastify/blob/0aef7f323a79835ae6529a4f72c90744a731c74e/fastify.js#L389-L395

This can be a point of discussion, would you mind opening an issue?
